# AGENTS.md

Rules for every agent that works in this toolkit. The toolkit holds skills that our teams install; it holds no
application code.

## Making a skill

1. A skill starts with its evals. Its cases go under `evals/skills/<name>/cases/`, one folder per case, each with
   a `case.json` and a `world/` folder. Nobody writes the skill's `SKILL.tmpl.md` until its cases have goldens and
   a baseline round without the skill has run.
2. Each skill gets at least eight trigger cases that should load it and eight near misses that should not. Each
   trigger case says whether it should load the skill and whether it is in the train or the test split, and half
   of each kind are in the test split.
3. Each skill gets at least two task cases, and each task case lists what a good run must show.
4. The goldens for a case are written by someone who did not write the case.
5. The eval owner runs every round. Nobody runs a round on cases they wrote, and nobody reports a result for a
   round that has not run.
6. A template cites the rules it applies by the IDs in `v2/rules/index.md` and never copies their text.

## Borrowing

- Read every file of a borrowed skill before you use any of it. Never run a borrowed script before it is reviewed.
- Copy text only when a licence covers the files you copy and allows it. With no such licence, copy nothing:
  write the skill new.
- For an adopted or adapted skill, record its repository, commit, path and licence in the template's `metadata`
  and in `THIRD_PARTY.md`, and keep any notice its licence asks for.

## Working rules

- Report only what you checked, and say what you did not check.
- Ask one clear question when a request is unclear, instead of guessing.

## Skills

| Skill | Path | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| release-notes | [v2/skills/release-notes/SKILL.tmpl.md](v2/skills/release-notes/SKILL.tmpl.md) | Writing the release notes for a tagged version from its merged pull requests. |
| pr-description-writer | [v2/skills/pr-description-writer/SKILL.tmpl.md](v2/skills/pr-description-writer/SKILL.tmpl.md) | Writing the description of a pull request from its branch. |

---
name: pr-description-writer
description: Drafts a pull request description from the branch. Use whenever an implementer opens a PR or asks for a PR write-up.
license: MIT
metadata:
  roles: implementer
  areas: rest
  sourcing: adapted
  source: github.com/example-user/pr-helper 4c1d9e2 skills/pr-helper/SKILL.md (MIT)
---

# PR description writer

Turn the work on the current branch into a description a reviewer can read within a couple of minutes.

## Before you write

1. Find where the branch left main and list every commit since then, oldest first (CORE-WORK-01).
2. List the files the branch changes, grouped by top-level folder.
3. Look for a linked issue in the branch name or the commit messages, and read it if there is one.
4. If the branch mixes two unrelated changes, tell the implementer and suggest splitting it before you write.

## Writing it

5. Start with a title in the imperative mood that would still read well in the release notes.
6. Open the body with one or two sentences on the problem this change solves, in words a user would use.
7. Under **What changed**, write one bullet for each area of the code, not one for each commit (CORE-SKILL-05).
8. Call out anything a reviewer could easily miss, such as a renamed setting or a changed default.
9. Under **How to test**, give the exact commands to run and what a passing run looks like.
10. Under **Risk**, mention anything that touches stored data, logins or a public API. If nothing does, write "Low".
11. Add screenshots only when the change alters something people see on screen.
12. Link the issue at the end with a closing keyword, so that it closes when the pull request is merged.

## Before you post

13. Read it once as the reviewer would, cut anything that only repeats the diff, and keep it under 300 words.
